_why: The Ops bot's 'give me a summary and suggest a resolution <intercom>' asks are 112 of the 301 asks Jan sent in 14 days, and each is followed by 'do resolution then update the user'. Today that resolution is an LLM-chosen production write in an agent turn. This file replaces the judgement with a LOOKUP: a closed intent vocabulary intersected with a closed fact pattern maps to exactly one action key, and an unmapped pair is 'unknown' (hand-off), never an improvised write. The suggestion a card prints NAMES the rule key below, so a wrong mapping is a one-line PR against this file, reviewable on its own.
_consumers: scripts/ops_intake/resolutions.py (the only reader; CI-checked by scripts/check-ops-resolutions.sh)
scripts/ops_intake/answer.py (turns a mapped W1 action into a WriteRequest; the router's step 9 is the only executor)
_editing: Adding an intent label or a fact predicate means adding it to INTENT_LABELS / PREDICATES in scripts/ops_intake/resolutions.py in the same PR — the loader fails closed on an unknown name, it never silently ignores a rule.

proof-review.describe: the document/claim proof verdict is decided by code (dv_outcomes), never here: hand the conversation to the proof-review lane

status-line.describe: post ONE answer-bank status line to the customer in the thread; it is a W1 write because it is a recorded, answer-bank-verbatim reply

gap-ask.describe: the dated proof ask has ONE sender; this surface hands the ask over instead of sending a second one

uvn-status.describe: the user_verification_needed status line has ONE sender; hand over, never send a second

erasure.describe: an erasure/takedown ask becomes a register row in the GDPR pipeline; this surface NEVER hides anything

erasure-store-missing.handoff: cannot check: the erasure store is not on this host - a human restores it; the customer is not asked again
erasure-store-missing.describe: the GDPR register could not be read, so whether this person was erased is UNKNOWN; a staff line names the host and path, and no customer ask is sent

merge-candidate.describe: run merge-verify.py in shadow, print its verdict and the exact command it recommends, and hand it to a named human; this surface never executes a merge

rename.describe: rename the profile the Intercom contact OWNS (r5) to the name the customer asked for; the inverse is the previous name, recorded on the ledger row before the write

billing.handoff: read-only Stripe card + the refund line for a named human
billing.describe: no refund and no cancellation leave this surface; the card shows the subscription state and the approved refund copy for a human

data-issue.describe: file/route the ClickUp ticket with a category; the ticket write is j-k1's

fraud-lens-ticket.describe: a 'this person is a fraudster, reject everything' report becomes a fraud-lens ticket and a hold review; NEVER a bulk status write

unknown.describe: no rule matched: page a human, and the page names the conversation id. No customer line is proposed from this surface: it cannot reassign a conversation (no reassignment writer is wired; router._production_writers() is empty by captain decision), the approved hand-off line is refused here by the output guard (promise/person_without_assignment) because it says a person is coming, and the approved honesty line (I have recorded this and will update you here as soon as there is news.) cannot be sent either: this reply path (scripts/intercom-ops-write.sh reply) does not write the owed_followup record that outbound.ts writes before that sentence, so posting it here would be an unbacked claim. The page is what stops the case going unattended

requester-linked-refusal.handoff: refuse and page: the target account is the requester's own, so every write here would be self-approval
requester-linked-refusal.describe: refuse the ask and page a human; no customer reply and no write

rules.why: the target account is the requester's own: every write here would be self-approval, so refuse and page - never a customer reply
2026-10-23 'Mixed by Big Boy': 'they are a fraudster, reject everything' must never become a bulk status write
a register row already exists and is open: the GDPR lane owns the next letter
the register is not on this host, so erasure is UNKNOWN: a human restores the store; asking the customer to prove their erasure again would make our failure their work
no register row yet: the ask is a new GDPR row, and this surface never hides anything
the row is closed; a closed row is re-read by the GDPR lane, not re-opened here
the erasure register holds a CLOSED row for this account, so the page really is hidden; the answer is the hidden_stays bank line and no new hide is due
no CLOSED erasure row was measured, so 'your page stays hidden' is a claim the register does not support: hand off instead of asserting it
user_verification_needed already has ONE sender (credit-review.py uvn-status); a second message is the double-send bug
the customer asks where the request is and code measures an open request: the answer-bank status line is true
no open request is measured, so a status line would be a promise about nothing: hand off
a document is on file for an open request: the decision belongs to the proof lane
no document is on file and the request is open: the dated ask has one sender
code measured a decline verdict: the answer is the approved decline line, never a fresh reason
no decline is measured: 'why was I rejected' is a proof/decision question
process question with an approved answer
process question with an approved answer
process question with an approved answer
the contact owns the profile per r5, so the rename is the customer's own name change
catalog pop >= 60 or >= 50 credits: a popular-profile rename is an impersonation surface, so a human does it
r5 does not resolve exactly one owning account: the rename is refused
no duplicate pair is measured for this account: nothing to verify yet
code measures a duplicate pair: merge-verify.py judges it and prints the command for a named human
no refund and no cancellation leave this surface
a wrong credit/name/metadata on the page is a data issue, not a status change
every other intent, or an unmeasured fact pattern: a human, by page (the hand-off line is guard-refused on a surface that cannot assign)
